adjudication_label: batch_3:dislocation density and elastic property relationships
canonical_question: Does a reduction in dislocation density typically lead to an increase in elastic modulus in FCC metals, or is this counter-intuitive behavior due to the HEA nature?

question_variants.question: Does a reduction in dislocation density typically lead to an increase in elastic modulus in FCC metals, or is this counter-intuitive behavior due to the HEA nature?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper reports an observation where a reduction in dislocation density at 600 K resulted in an increase in elastic modulus (from 173 GPa to 219 GPa). It does not discuss whether this behavior is typical for FCC metals or specific to the HEA nature, leaving the generalization to standard FCC metals unanswered based solely on the provided text.

answers.answer: In the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating simulation, the density of dislocations at 600 K was significantly reduced compared with that at 300 K, resulting in an increase of the elastic modulus of the material from 173 GPa to 219 GPa. The text does not provide a comparison to standard FCC metals to determine if this is counter-intuitive or typical.
answers.material: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on Cu matrix
answers.measurement_outcome: dislocation density reduced; elastic modulus increased (173 GPa -> 219 GPa)
answers.mechanism: reduced dislocation density leading to increased elastic modulus
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparison to standard FCC metals provided to establish general behavior.
evidence_spans: In this study, the wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating was systematically analyzed by the molecular dynamics method.
The friction and nanoindentation simulation of this coating material were carried out by controlling the ambient temperature.

The results show that with the increase of temperature, the disorder of the lattice structure increases, which leads to an increase of the tangential force and friction coefficient in the friction process.
